summary: Serinity Young was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. She earned her Ph.D. from Columbia University in 1990 under Alex Wayman and studied under Vidya Dehejia, later working at the American Museum of Natural History and Southern Methodist University in 2000.
Seung-yeon Lee works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. Lee completed doctoral studies under Sang-hae Lee and held posts at Sungkyunkwan University and the Gyeonggi Cultural Foundation.

Seunghak Koh is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned an MA from Seoul National University and a PhD from UCLA in 2011 under Robert E. Buswell Jr. Koh has served as an Appointed Researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Seán McLoughlin is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed a Ph.D. at the University of Manchester. In 2005, he was attested as Lecturer in South Asian, Islamic and Religious Studies at the University of Leeds.

Shailendra Bhandare specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held positions at the British Museum and Fitzwilliam Museum, and served at the Ashmolean Museum (attested 2006–2022) and as a Fellow at St Cross College, Oxford (attested 2022).
Shan Shan Zhao is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a Master of Arts at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn, also studying under Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.
Shane McCausland is a scholar in sinology and history and archaeology. He studied at Princeton University from 1996 to 2000 and took up a post at SOAS University of London in 2009.
Shanshan Jia is an Indology scholar who was attested in 2015 as a doctoral student at the University of Hamburg under the supervision of Harunaga Isaacson.

Shaoyong Ye is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies at Peking University in 2009 under Qing Duan and served there as an Associate Professor (attested 2010–2016).
Sharon J. Roe is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who earned a PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies under the supervision of Steven D. Goodman (attested 2014).
Sharon Salzberg is a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar. She studied at the University at Buffalo from circa 1969 to 1971 and under traditional teacher Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche circa 1971.

Shashibhusan Dasgupta was an Indian scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Scottish Church College and the University of Calcutta, where he later served as a Lecturer from circa 1945 to 1964.

Shayne Clarke specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Bukkyo University, the University of Canterbury (MA under Paul Harrison), and UCLA (PhD 2006 under Gregory Schopen), later becoming an Associate Professor at McMaster University (attested 2015–2016).
Shek-wing Tam was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under traditional teacher Dudjom Rinpoche from circa 1972 to 1987 and held a post at Renmin University of China.

Sheldon Pollock is an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Harvard University (~1971–1975). He held posts at the University of Iowa (~1977–1989), University of Chicago (~1989–2005), Columbia University (~2005), and Clay Sanskrit Library (~2005–2008).

Sheng Yen was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Rissho University (~1969–1975) under Dongchu. He founded Dharma Drum Mountain, held a post at Chung-Hwa Institute of Buddhist Studies (~1985–2009), and taught at National Cheng Kung University.

Shenghai Li specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Li earned a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Donald R. Davis Jr., also studying with Charles Hallisey, Gudrun Bühnemann, Ram Shankar Tripathi, H. V. Nagaraja Rao, and several Tibetan traditional teachers.

Shenpen Hookham is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under multiple traditional Tibetan teachers and earned a D.Phil from the University of Oxford (~1980–1986) under doctoral supervisor Michael M. Broido.

Shi Huifeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under K. L. Dhammajoti. He held academic posts at the University of Hong Kong and Fo Guang University, where he was a professor (attested 2013).

Shichang Ma was a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He worked as a Buddhist archaeology researcher at Dunhuang Academy (1963–1978) and held a post in the Archaeology Department at Peking University beginning in 1982.
